text:
Jordan (CS): flagging urgent customer reports: multiple customers (Meridian Systems, HealthBridge, Ledgerly) filed escalations ~30-90m ago complaining that retrieval + reranking outputs degraded after last night's optimizer rollout. common themes: missing explicit citations in answers, lower recall on policy/legal doc lookups, and fewer top_k hits returned. customers provided repros and want mitigation.

Ops Bot: created tickets TKT-4999, TKT-5000, TKT-5001 and linked to this thread.

Priya (Support Eng): Meridian provided a concise repro (curl):
```
POST /v1/retrieve
{ "query": "required documentation for tax exemption claim", "top_k": 7 }
# then
POST /v1/rerank
{ "items": ["MS-101","MS-234",...], "reranker_model": "rwd-rerank-2026-03b", "mode": "semantic-hybrid" }
```
They say doc MS-101 (explicit table of evidence with section refs) used to appear in top3 and now is missing entirely.

Alex (Eng-ML): we rolled optimizer canary canary-2026-03-14-opt2 last night; deploy log below. curious if embed or reranker variants changed vector geometry or scoring. please paste before/after outputs and index settings.

Deploy Bot: Canary canary-2026-03-14-opt2 started by @ci/cd at 2026-03-14T22:58:45Z, rollout to 100% completed at 2026-03-14T23:42:19Z, commit sha: e4f9b7c

Jordan (CS): Meridian example snapshots:
Before (archived):
```
retrieve: ["MS-101","MS-234","MS-412"],
rerank: [{"id":"MS-101","score":0.95,"snippet":"Section 2.4: Documentation required for tax exemption..."}]
```
After (now):
```
retrieve: ["MS-234","MS-412","MS-879"],
rerank: [{"id":"MS-234","score":0.78,"snippet":"Applicant eligibility and forms..."}]
# MS-101 is ranked 10+ or absent
```
Index: HNSW m=24 ef_construction=200 ef_search=96. embedding: rwd-embed-4.1 (v2026-03b).

Theo (Runtime): quick ops notes: canary included a vector shard compaction and a new near-duplicate filter (sim_threshold=0.74 previously 0.86). compaction may have pruned low-recall partitions and the sim_threshold lowering makes dedupe more aggressive. rolling a config revert is quick if desired.

Alex (Eng-ML): running a small eval on a 18-query failing set provided by customers. preliminary numbers:
- embed v2026-02 + rerank v2026-02 (baseline): recall@7 = 0.84, MRR = 0.66
- embed v2026-03b + rerank v2026-03b (rolled): recall@7 = 0.49, MRR = 0.36
- embed v2026-03b + rerank v2026-02: recall@7 = 0.63, MRR = 0.52
- embed v2026-02 + rerank v2026-03b: recall@7 = 0.56, MRR = 0.41
Interpretation: embedding change accounts for the majority of recall loss; reranker change exacerbates ranking of the wrong docs.

Priya (Support Eng): customers also reported generator outputs losing citation anchors when the system assembles context from top_k results. HealthBridge said summaries now cite generic paragraphs instead of linking to the original policy sections. they flagged compliance impact.

Theo (Runtime): mitigation options (fast to slow): 1) revert near-duplicate sim_threshold to 0.86 via config flag (minutes) 2) route affected customers to fallback model pair (embed+rerank v2026-02) via routing rules (minutes) 3) reindex with normalization or run model-side fix (hours) 4) full model rollback (longer). what do we want first?

Sarah (note: product not present in this thread) - N/A

Alex (Eng-ML): model training notes show v2026-03b introduced per-batch scale augmentation that shifts vector norms; we didn't apply L2-normalization at index/search in all customer indexes. options: apply search-time normalization shim (cheap, immediate), reindex with normalized vectors (costly), or adjust model to remove augmentation. search-side normalization recovers most nearest-neighbor matches in a quick offline test.

Priya (Support Eng): customers asked for ETA and mitigation now. I'm recommending: 1) apply routing for Meridian/HealthBridge/Ledgerly to fallback embed+rerank v2026-02 2) revert sim_threshold to 0.86 3) deploy search-side normalization shim to a small canary and measure recall/citation coverage for 1h. provide customers update within 3 hours.

Theo (Runtime): applied routing rule RTE-131 to Meridian and HealthBridge at 2026-03-15T00:12:07Z (traffic -> embed+rerank v2026-02). reverted sim_threshold on cluster-04 at 2026-03-15T00:15:30Z. monitoring shows top_k counts returned per-query increased back toward baseline.

Alex (Eng-ML): ran a quick experiment: adding search-time L2-normalization to queries with embed v2026-03b recovered recall@7 to 0.80 on the failing harness without reindexing. created PR #1893 for the normalization shim and unit regression tests. reindex estimate for Ledgerly-sized index: 1.5-4 hours.

Priya (Support Eng): drafted customer message for Meridian/HealthBridge/Ledgerly: "We identified a regression in retrieval relevance after a recent optimizer update. We've routed your traffic to a verified fallback and reverted an aggressive dedupe setting. We're also testing a fast mitigation to normalize vectors at search time; we expect to confirm results within 12 hours and will follow up with a timeline for a permanent fix." asked legal to scan for wording. customers acknowledged and asked to be notified before any reindex. :thumbsup:

Ops Bot: tickets TKT-4999/TKT-5000/TKT-5001 updated: status=mitigated (fallback routing + sim_threshold revert), next_update=2026-03-15T10:00:00Z.

Theo (Runtime): creating a temporary dashboard for recall@k, citation-coverage, and per-customer top_k counts. also adding an alert: recall_delta > 0.12 for >30m. will post link.

Alex (Eng-ML): owners: Alex -> lead on PR/shim and validation harness, Theo -> routing/configs/ops, Priya -> customer communication and ticket updates. will post PR link and canary results here when ready.

Jordan (CS): thanks all. customers are on fallback and appreciative of the swift mitigation. Priya, once shim passes canary and we have numbers, we'll coordinate a window for reindexing if needed. keep me posted so I can run their test queries before we flip them back.

Ops Bot: note: deploy metadata for canary canary-2026-03-14-opt2 recorded for rollback path.
